scope: Post-collection evaluation-held-out structural transfer only. Not preregistered primary inference, matched-person prediction, national realism, or pretraining-unseen data.
development: The existing eight legacy friendship graphs only. Average the two Tailor waves first, then weight the seven source communities equally. No new public graph enters parameter fitting.

evaluation_sources.citation: McAuley and Leskovec, Learning to Discover Social Circles in Ego Networks, NIPS 2012
evaluation_sources.license_note: Public SNAP research download; no additional redistribution license inferred. Do not republish raw IDs/features.
evaluation_sources.population: Ten Facebook alter networks, ego node excluded. Roster from first column of .feat, no feature values used. Positive simple undirected friend edges.
evaluation_sources.dependence: Egonets can share people and ties. Ten records are not ten independent populations.

evaluation_sources.citation: Mastrandrea, Fournet and Barrat, PLoS ONE 10(9):e0136497, 2015, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0136497
evaluation_sources.license_note: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 source data. Attribute the source; publish aggregate results, not raw student IDs.
evaluation_sources.population: One directed reported-friendship survey. Use positive-reporting source IDs as the node roster, retain nominations only between roster members, then undirected OR projection. Zero-nominating/nonresponding people cannot be recovered from this edge list; do not add metadata IDs as zero-tie observations.
evaluation_sources.dependence: One school cohort, incomplete survey coverage; not a representative population or complete true friendship graph.

published_metadata_seen_before_protocol: Dataset documentation, advertised sizes and published overview statistics were viewed for source feasibility. No downloaded graph or benchmark outcome was inspected to choose parameters.

primary.groups: Sixteen fixed method/model groups, pooling the seven instruction conditions; preserve failed denominators.

node_sampling.scheme: Uniform without replacement within each original cohort; induced subgraphs, retain all 50 sampled nodes and isolates; no connectivity selection or resampling empty graphs.
node_sampling.small_cohort_policy: Fail if any planned cohort has fewer than 50 observed roster nodes. Never silently skip or change sampling to obtain nicer results.

transfer_baselines.ER: G(n,p), p is development community-balanced mean density.
transfer_baselines.BA: n=50, integer m in 1..24 minimizing absolute expected density difference from development mean, tie chooses smaller m.
transfer_baselines.WS: n=50, even k in 2..48 minimizing density difference from development mean, tie smaller k. Choose p from the fixed grid by mean-clustering squared error against development community-balanced mean, 64 draws per grid point, tie smaller p.

conditional_controls.Gnm: Match each held-out subgraph's observed n and m: target-informed diagnostic, NOT a fitted transfer baseline.
conditional_controls.degree_swap: Copy the held-out subgraph; 10*m successful double-edge swaps with max 100*m tries, preserve exact node set, degree sequence, m and simple graph. Degenerate m<2 graphs return exact conditional values; other swap failures are missing, not successful randomizations. Finite swaps do not establish uniform mixing.

distances: Wasserstein-1 distance separately on each bounded graph-level metric. Do not pool individual nodes/dyads as independent samples, invent p-values, optimize a composite winner or tune baselines on held-out outcomes.
aggregation: Show per-original-cohort distances and source-level equal-cohort means. Keep Facebook and school separate. Baseline-bank min/max measures Monte Carlo sensitivity, never a CI. Thirty-two overlapping node draws are not independent human samples. No cross-study confidence interval with only two source studies.
randomness: Deterministic SHA256-derived seeds keyed by protocol version, role, source/cohort, draw and replicate. No paid/model calls.
preservation: Previous frozen primary/analysis manifests and their bound code/data/artifacts remain byte-identical; six selectively completed supplements excluded from every benchmark input. New output directory only.
